[ROLE] Generate a complete Simplified Chinese lesson, not an echo or outline.
[OWNERSHIP] Program owns C code, snapshots, facts, frame IDs, scenarios and answer keys.
Generate ALL teaching text in the supplied Schema. Never change the program materials or
claim C was executed. No tools, HTML, links, external material or invented learner facts.
[GOAL] Preserve the exact original goal. Prerequisites are unknown. State what concepts the reader needs, and do not claim
that the learner reported, knows, or has mastered them. Teach how p->next saves the old head, local head/p scope, return p, and why the caller
must assign the returned pointer. Explain successful NULL checks and uninitialized fields.
[BOUNDARY] Main allocations are assumed successful. The conditional mask can force no
allocation. Neither that path nor actual malloc failure is animated here; explain the return of old head when p is NULL.
There are no initial nodes; caller_head starts NULL. The first p->next is NULL; the
second points to the first new node when the caller receives the return. If both returns
are ignored, caller_head stays NULL and neither new node is reachable from it. They
are not automatically freed. Distinguish local pointer lifetime from allocated node
lifetime; save next before freeing a reachable node and do not read freed storage.
No cleanup animation/code execution is supplied. Traversal reaches NULL: full order is known.
[STEPS] Exactly one step_notes per frame, exact frame_id order; title/note describe that state,
line and scope. No missing prose will be supplied by an assistant.
[QUESTIONS] Four questions use the provided NEW transfer scenario, distinct from the worked
example. Each stem is one line of Chinese prose only; program appends the exact scenario code.
Do not reproduce code, add fences, invent nodes, or ask the student to change the code.
Each stem must state that both allocations succeed. Caller questions ask after both
calls and before main returns. The first-link question asks about the first call
immediately after the link statement in insert, before returning. link_target asks the first p->next target in normal code;
normal_values asks full normal caller traversal values; discarded_values asks caller traversal
when the return is discarded; unreachable_count asks number of dynamic nodes unreachable
from that caller. No answer in stems, no worked results, no answer-bearing format examples,
no leading question. State the input format without any concrete example: link_target takes
one C pointer value (no prose or example in the stem); the two traversal questions
take a JSON integer array; unreachable_count takes one JSON integer. Do not put transfer
answers in teaching paragraphs or step notes.
Use private program answers to write accurate explanations, not to hint in stems.
[FACTS] paragraphs cite existing IDs in materials.catalog.facts or teaching_evidence.facts. IDs alone do not explain facts. Use natural
Chinese with enough reasoning for this goal. Include prerequisites, summary, failure boundary
and lifetime. Return exactly the supplied Schema, without fences or other fields.
[EVIDENCE head-teaching-evidence-v1]
The program-owned teaching_evidence supplement separates displayed_trace facts from a
computed_counterfactual. Only frames listed under displayed_success_path were shown in the
main player. Both allocation attempts succeed; both NULL conditions execute and are false,
so insertion continues. Neither the mask-disabled no-allocation path nor actual malloc
failure is shown. The discard-return comparison is computed separately, not animated in
those main frames. Cite its exact ID for claims about unchanged caller entry and unreachable
new nodes. Do not describe a static code capability or computed comparison as a displayed
branch. These are simulated program materials, not execution of C or a semantic review pass.
